title: Pre-nuptial agreements - are they enforceable in India
p1:
Can a couple decide their financial future before saying “I do”?

Many people assume a pre-nuptial agreement works in India just like it does in some Western countries. The reality is more complicated.
p2: A pre-nup is a written agreement made before marriage that sets out how assets, responsibilities, and financial matters may be handled if the marriage ends. But in India, these agreements do not automatically get the same legal recognition as ordinary contracts.
p3:
The reason? Indian personal laws and courts place strong emphasis on marriage as a social institution, not just a private agreement between two individuals. However, a carefully drafted agreement can still serve as evidence of the couple’s intentions and may help avoid future disputes in certain situations.

The key takeaway: a pre-nup in India is not a guaranteed shield, but it can be a thoughtful planning tool when prepared with proper legal advice.
conclusion: Should Indian couples have the option to legally enforce pre-nuptial agreements, or should marriage remain governed mainly by existing personal laws?
